raw:
I haven't checked these against the benchmark data. They come from what I recall of NAS-Bench-201 behaviour. Most of them rest on one pattern: adding a conv to an edge that is currently `none` gains more than swapping one op for another, and removing a conv costs more than removing a pool or skip. The last two use cross-edge conditions based on my recollection that a skip on edge 3 (0→3) already provides a residual path. That makes extra convs on the other edges into the output less valuable.
